To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified six molecular species of CEOOH and confirmed their presence in VLDL, IDL and plasma.

the molecular species of cholesterly ester hydroperoxide were detected in very low-density (VLDL, 1.006 < density < 1.063 g/mL) and intermediate-density (IDL, 1.063 < density <1.210 g/mL) lipoprotein fractions in human plasma.

the presence of molecular cholesteryl esters hydroperoxides was confirmed in very low density and intermediate density lipoproteins with analytical sensitivity of 10-12 mol, showing the constant presence of more molecular cholesteryl hydroperoxides species in intermediate density lipoprotein than in very low density lipoprotein.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and quantification of cholesteryl linoleate hydroperoxides, a major product of the oxidation of cholesteryl oleate in human plasma lipoproteins by using a highly sensitive liquid chromatographymass spectrometer.

the detection and identification of molecular species of CEOOH present in VLDL, IDL and plasma by using liquid chromatography/LtQ ion trap mass specrometry/Orbtirap high mass accuracy mass specrometry.
the detection and identification of CEOHs in VLDL, IDL and plasma by using highly sensitive LC/MS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study has identified the presence of CEOOH in VLDL, IDL and plasma of human donors, and has provided a novel biochemical evidence for the role of these lipoprotein species in atherogenesis.
the presence of CEOOHs in VLDLs and IDLs was confirmed with analytical sensitivity of 1.0 pmol, and more CEOOH species were present in IDLs than VLDLs.
the present study provides a novel finding of the presence of CEOOH in VLDL, IDL, and plasma, and the constant appearance of CEOOH in IDL and plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of CEOOH in triglyceride-rich plasma and lipoprotein particles, such as VLDL and LDL, is a novel finding that might be related to the pathophysiology of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease.
the presence of CEOOH in VLDL/IDL is a potential risk for the development of atherosclerosis, and that this is the first report to show that the presence of more CEOOH in IDL than in VLDL.
we have identified the molecular species of cholesteroyl ester hydroperoxide in very low-density or intermediate-density lipoprotein, and these lipoprotein species might have atherogenic potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified molecular species of cholesterly ester hydroperoxide (CEOOH), namely, Ch20: 5-OOH in very low-density (VLDL, intermediate-density lipoprotein (IDL) and in plasma.
the presence of CEOOH in triglyceride-rich VLDL and intermediate-density lipids (IDL) was confirmed with the high analytical sensitivity.

the presence of cholesteryl linoleate hydroperoxide (CE 20:4-00H) and cholesteryl arachidonate hydroperoxide in very low-density (VLDL), intermediate-density (IDL) lipoproteins, and plasma is demonstrated by using highly sensitive mass spectrometry.
